clue.text: The people generally in church services

definitions.meaning: ordinary folk taken as a whole, the populace
celebrations of the Eucharist, especially Catholic ones

explanation.surface: A remark that ordinary people are to be found at church.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: the common populace, and Eucharistic worship, plural.

clue.text: Crew on singular boat abandoned in part of Canada

parts.note: to crew a ship is to man it
I is the singular first person

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild disorder, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A crew leaves a lone boat somewhere in Canada.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' reads as the crew deserting ship, but it signals a shuffle, giving ITOBA.
explanation.definitionFit: A prairie province in central Canada, with Winnipeg as its capital.

clue.text: Placed duties at random

indicators.note: random signals that the letters of duties at are scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Tasks have been handed out haphazardly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something located or positioned somewhere has been placed there.

clue.text: A daughter in flight — what an adventure!

indicators.note: in places the article and the daughter abbreviation inside the word for flight

parts.note: flight, a getaway, is an escape

explanation.surface: A daughter's runaway journey is quite an adventure.
explanation.definitionFit: A daring or mischievous exploit is a madcap adventure.

clue.text: Inactive sort of investor facing new worker

parts.note: a stag is a speculator who buys new shares to sell quickly
the ant is the crossword's stock worker insect

explanation.surface: A dormant kind of investor sitting opposite a newly hired employee.
explanation.walkthrough: A STAG is a stock-market speculator who applies for new share issues to sell at once for profit.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water or trade is still and sluggish, without movement.

clue.text: Offer to pay for novice in America

parts.note: to tender is to offer formally
to foot a bill is to pay for it

explanation.surface: An offer to cover costs for a newcomer to America.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition flags that the word is chiefly American usage for a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: An inexperienced newcomer, originally to the frontier, is a greenhorn.

clue.text: A quick look for a bird

explanation.definitionFit: A brief glance in slang, and the male of the goose.

clue.text: Humiliated by article on foundation day

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
a foundation is a base

explanation.surface: Someone shamed by a newspaper article on Founders' Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone abased has been lowered in dignity, degraded.

clue.text: Takes steps to start studies

indicators.note: start takes the opening letter of the word to

parts.note: to study a subject at university is to read it

explanation.surface: A student takes action to begin studying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start' takes T from 'to'; READS is the British sense of studying at university.
explanation.definitionFit: Walking with steps, placing feet down, is what one does when one treads.

clue.text: Observe books in pleasant surroundings

indicators.note: the word for pleasant surrounds the books abbreviation, holding it within

parts.note: pleasant means nice
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An invitation to watch books in an agreeable setting.
explanation.definitionFit: To spot or take note of something is to observe it.

clue.text: Untie and release flood

indicators.note: release suggests freeing the letters of the two words to fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to untie something and let it go, causing a flood.
explanation.definitionFit: To deluge or swamp something with water is to flood it.

clue.text: Walks for miles — into ambushes!

indicators.note: into says the miles abbreviation goes inside the word for ambushes

parts.note: ambushes are traps

explanation.surface: Hikers walk for miles and straight into an ambush.
explanation.definitionFit: Long tiring hikes are tramps, so a verb or plural noun for trudging journeys.

clue.text: Clergyman who will always finish on the right

parts.note: always means ever
finish means end

explanation.surface: A priest who insists on ending up on the right side, politically.
explanation.definitionFit: The title given to a priest or minister, used as a noun for one.

clue.text: Inspired, found heart in the final

indicators.note: in places the word for heart within the word for the final

parts.note: the final is the end
heart means courage, pluck

explanation.surface: A team found its fighting spirit in the cup final.
explanation.definitionFit: Being given heart or confidence, emboldened, is the same as being spurred on.

clue.text: A useful implement for cutting money?

definitions.text: A useful implement for cutting money?

parts.words: A useful implement for cutting money?
parts.note: money is slangily dough or loaf, so a blade for slicing it is a kitchen tool for loaves

explanation.walkthrough: BREAD is slang for money, so a tool that cuts 'bread' becomes a pun on a kitchen blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated kitchen blade made for slicing loaves.

clue.text: West to call — impossible squeeze!

parts.note: to ring is to call by phone
out, as in out of the question, means impossible

explanation.surface: Phoning from the West is ruled out by a tight budget.
explanation.definitionFit: To press water from a cloth by twisting is to squeeze it dry.

clue.text: Goodbye from rayon as a material?

indicators.note: material, with its query, hints that the letters of rayon as a are the stuff to be remade

explanation.surface: A farewell made from rayon fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: The Japanese word for farewell is in common English use.
explanation.definitionFit: Japanese for farewell, borrowed into English as a parting word.

clue.text: The way to be able to buy a town?

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to afford something is to have the means to buy it

explanation.surface: A question about how to get the money to buy a whole town.
explanation.walkthrough: STAFFORD is the county town of Staffordshire in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: The county town of Staffordshire in England.

clue.text: Quick to show embarrassment from clothes labelled thus?

definitions.text: Quick to show embarrassment from clothes labelled thus?

parts.words: Quick to show embarrassment from clothes labelled thus?
parts.note: blushing is showing a hue, and fast means quick; garments with this label keep their dye in the wash

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words, COLOUR (blush) plus FAST (quick); a care label with the word promises the dye will not run.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric whose dye does not wash out or fade is described this way on its label.

clue.text: Lots of idle drawings are executed

indicators.note: executed means beheaded, so the first letter of the scribbles comes off

parts.note: doodles are aimless sketches

explanation.surface: Many aimless scribbles get done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are executed' beheads DOODLES, removing its first letter D.
explanation.definitionFit: Oodles means a great quantity, plenty.

clue.text: A trusted advisor for people on the rise?

parts.note: people means men
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: A counsellor for those on the way up in their careers.
explanation.walkthrough: A TOR is a rocky hilltop, common on Dartmoor in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A guide and confidant who coaches a less experienced person.

clue.text: Reach for a dry article at home

parts.note: TT means teetotal, so dry
a is the indefinite article
at home means in

explanation.surface: Grasping for a dry thing lying around the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To attain a goal is to reach or achieve it.

clue.text: Some cricket shot causing upset!

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket
a shot, a go, is a turn

explanation.surface: A cricket stroke that causes an upset in the match.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is a set of six deliveries bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To upset something is to knock it over or reverse it, as a verb.

clue.text: Unique occasion — only ten players on!

definitions.meaning: a single event that will not be repeated
a team of eleven reduced by a sending-off has one player missing

explanation.surface: A football match turns into a one-time event after a red card.
explanation.walkthrough: Football and cricket teams have eleven players, so ten on the field means one sent off.
explanation.definitionFit: A special event happening a single time, versus a team short of one player.

clue.text: Greatly disturbed about hospital inertia

indicators.note: about says the rearranged letters go round the hospital abbreviation
disturbed means the letters of greatly are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply upset by the sluggishness at a hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' turns GREATLY into LETARGY, and 'about' puts that round H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is sluggishness, a lack of energy, the same idea as torpor.

clue.text: Author oddly chasing cat from the fruit

indicators.note: chasing puts the author letters behind the cat, following it

parts.note: a tom is a male cat

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of author

explanation.surface: An author chases a cat away from a piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the' is only a link: the definition is just 'fruit', and 'oddly' and 'chasing' do the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a berry, it is a red fruit commonly treated as a salad vegetable.

clue.text: Are needs transformed by such a song?

indicators.note: transformed means the letters of are needs are reshaped into a new word

explanation.surface: A question whether a song can change what someone needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A love song sung beneath a window at night is a classic example of this kind of song.

clue.text: Bear crossing river with abandon

indicators.note: crossing has the word for bear lying across the river abbreviation, so holding it

parts.note: to bear something is to stand it

explanation.surface: A bear wades over a river with reckless abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand someone is to leave them stranded, deserting them.
